title: Head-on situation: which way do you turn? COLREG Rule 14 explained

scenes.label: WHO GIVES WAY?
scenes.heading: Head-on at sea. Which way do you turn?
scenes.narration: Two power-driven vessels are meeting head-on. Which way do you turn?

scenes.label: RULE 14
scenes.heading: Both vessels alter course to starboard
scenes.narration: You see a vessel ahead, on a reciprocal course. By night you see both her sidelights, and her masthead lights in a line. Rule 14 is clear: each vessel alters course to starboard, so that they pass port to port.

scenes.label: WHAT THE RULES REQUIRE
scenes.heading: Three things to remember

items.title: In doubt? Assume it exists
items.text: Rule 14(c): treat it as head-on and act

items.title: Make it obvious
items.text: A large, early alteration with one short blast

scenes.narration: In a head-on situation there is no stand-on vessel. Both must act. If you are in any doubt whether the situation exists, assume that it does. And make your alteration large and early, with one short blast.

scenes.label: KEY TAKEAWAY
scenes.heading: Head-on: alter to starboard, pass port to port.
scenes.narration: Head-on means alter to starboard, and pass port to port.
